items.headline: 安大略湖擬改名美國湖
items.context: 美國內政部長表示，蘋果公司在與川普總統會談後，可能跟進把地圖上的「安大略湖」（Lake Ontario）改名為「美國湖」（Lake America）。這場改名風波，先前 Google 已經在週末替美國用戶的地圖改了名，但另一家地圖業者 MapQuest 表示不會跟進。

sources.summary: Great Park, Irvine, California Performances from Rodrigo, Stevie Nicks, Chappell Roan and Sarah McLachlan raise $20m for charity yet are marred by poor planning for heatwave Shortly after singing the closing notes of her indie pop gem LES Artistes on Saturday afternoon, Santigold gazes out at the sweat-laced crowd at the Daisy Chain Fields festival – a benefit concert hosted by Olivia Rodrigo for charities focused on women and girls – in disbelief. “I can’t believe she pulled this shit off!” Santigold cries into the microphone, beaming. The inaugural festival, Great Park in Irvine, California, has drawn in 45,000 people to see artists as varied as the legendary punk agitators Bikini Kill , kicky pop phenom Chappell Roan and kinetic superstar rapper Doechii , all of whom agreed to perform free of charge; Rodrigo herself closes out the night with a career-spanning setlist and starry guest appearances. The festival raised $10m to be distributed evenly among 10 non-profits, including Baby2Baby, which distributes supplies to children and parents in need, and the National Women’s Law Center. Later that night, Melinda French Gates joins Rodrigo on stage and matches the fundraising, bringing the donated total to $20m. Continue reading...

items.context: 這次帶大家看幾則《衛報》的最新評論：警匪影集《Vigil》第三季評價普通，前首相布朗（Gordon Brown）談民粹主義的新書獲得好評，紀錄片《Bel》則回顧一位早逝創作歌手的一生。
items.thread_text: 這次帶大家看幾則《衛報》最新的文化評論。警匪影集《Vigil》來到第三季，故事場景搬到北極圈的斯瓦爾巴群島，動作場面不少，但評論說主角個性太平淡，很難讓人投入。英國前首相布朗（Gordon Brown）出了一本新書《The Future Starts With Us》，談如何用地方層級的互助對抗民粹主義，評論形容這本書態度樂觀、立場清楚。另外，紀錄片《Bel》回顧創作歌手歐登尤（Beldina Odenyo）的一生，她在流亡、失落與種族歧視的傷痛中寫出音樂，卻在 2021 年不幸過世，紀錄片細膩地記錄了她生前最後的錄音過程。本則整理自衛報多個版面的報導。

sources.summary: Suranne Jones and Rose Leslie are back trying to stop a third world war in the Arctic. There’s plenty of action – but it’s hard to root for heroes whose biggest personality traits are ‘being nice’ and ‘wears good glasses’ Like many a police procedural, Vigil always begins with a cold open. This time round, however, it’s absolutely freezing. We are, as per, thrown headlong into a niche and tangentially Scottish military world where a murder has occurred. The first series took place on board a nuclear submarine (the show is, confusingly, still named after the vessel), while the second split the action between an army airfield in Scotland and the fictional Middle Eastern nation of Wudyan. For its third outing, we find ourselves in the (real) Arctic region of Svalbard. The area is supposedly demilitarised, but four British special forces agents are working undercover at a research centre, and tonight their mission is to extract a Chinese scientist who has made a discovery that could either save or destroy the world. En route, they’re ambushed by Russians who want whatever world-saving-or-destroying stuff she’s got. The scientist escapes – but one of the Brits later turns up dead in a Russian enclave. sources.summary: Global crises are tightly linked to how we treat each other at the local level, argues this optimistic book In times of crisis, there is one person to whom the left still turns for guidance. More than a decade and a half after leaving government, Gordon Brown has mellowed into the Labour party’s favourite wise elder; one who has never disappointed the faithful by going off to make a ton of money, remaining quietly committed to public service and deeply engaged with the world’s knottier problems. Having successfully led the global response to the financial crash of 2008, and advocated powerfully during the pandemic for global cooperation against the virus, he was never going to simply sit back and shrug as the world spiralled into conflict and chaos under Donald Trump. sources.summary: Beldina Odenyo alchemised the pain of exile, loss and racism into music as Heir of the Cursed before her death in 2021, as this attentive tribute explores Instead of an artist in a booth, a lone amplifier plays the music of singer-songwriter Beldina Odenyo for a cluster of microphones to pick up during the posthumous recording of her debut album. It is a haunting encapsulation of the absence and presence at the heart of Louise Lockwood’s documentary, which makes a commendably thorough exploration of the mental illness that led to Odenyo killing herself in November 2021, and its roots: exile, loss and racism. Performing under the moniker Heir of the Cursed, a translation of the Tetela name of assassinated Congolese leader Patrice Lumumba , Odenyo was on the verge of bigger recognition at the end of 2021 after a successful performance at Edinburgh’s Usher Hall. But hemmed in by successive Covid lockdowns, the 31-year-old is clearly unwell in a discomfiting backstage interview. Squirming, monosyllabic, she seems to be regressing to the non-verbal state of shock in which she arrived in Dumfriesshire from Kenya as a young child. Continue reading...

items.context: 輝達（Nvidia）宣布投資 35 億美元入股台灣晶片廠聯發科（MediaTek），這筆投資被視為輝達因應大型科技公司自研 AI 晶片浪潮的布局，希望繼續在 AI 基礎建設中占有一席之地。

items.context: 英格蘭銀行總裁貝利（Andrew Bailey）向 G20 提出警告，AI 產業的「波動性」，加上美伊戰爭引發的能源衝擊，可能導致全球經濟陷入衰退。
